Complementary information — The documents provide different measurements and contexts for comparing vitamin C in strawberries and oranges, all agreeing strawberries have more but using varying serving sizes and units.

The evidence clusters by different measurement units and serving sizes, all supporting the same core claim. d1, d3, and d8 give vitamin C per cup of strawberries (85mg, 89mg) versus per medium orange (70mg). d2 gives per 100g (59mg for strawberries vs. less for oranges). d4, d5, d6, and d7 make general comparative statements without specific numbers. All non-irrelevant documents (d1-d8) agree strawberries have more vitamin C than oranges; the differences are in the specific quantities and serving definitions, which are complementary details.

All retrieved documents support the claim that strawberries have more vitamin C than oranges, though they present complementary information using different measurements (per cup, per 100g, per serving) and some include general statements. The combined evidence from d1, d2, d3, d4, d5, d7, and d8 consistently shows strawberries exceed oranges in vitamin C content.

Yes, strawberries have more vitamin C than oranges. Multiple sources confirm this using different measurements: a cup of strawberries provides about 85-89 mg of vitamin C, compared to about 70 mg in a medium orange [d1][d3][d8]. Another source states that per 100g, strawberries contain 59 mg of vitamin C, which is more than the amount in 100g of oranges [d2]. General statements also note strawberries have more vitamin C by weight or per serving than citrus fruits [d4][d5][d7].
